title: Workload benchmarks and integration briefing — Cygnus Mobility POC
summary: POC scoping to validate latency & throughput for in-vehicle assistant use cases, define success criteria and sprint timeline. Agreement on 4-week pilot, openai-compatible endpoints + SDK integration, structured JSON outputs for telemetry, and benchmark plan to run on Redwood Dedicated/Private variants. Action items: Redwood to send benchmark template and initial load scripts; Cygnus to provide sample corpus and target SLOs; schedule infra kickoff next week.
topics: Function/tool calling and structured output (JSON schemas)
Deployment options: Dedicated vs Private VPC
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and load scripts (drive link)
Cygnus to provide 10k example queries + telemetry schema by 2027-01-03
Schedule infra kick-off with Cygnus SRE (week of 2027-01-04)
Redwood to propose Dedicated vs Private cost/latency comparison by 2027-01-06
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share benchmark template + security brief (due 2027-01-02)
Maya Patel: Prep example deployment config + default SDK snippets (due 2027-01-04)
Priya Desai: Export sample corpus and telemetry schema (due 2027-01-03)
Marco Ruiz: Confirm VPC peering constraints and firewall rules (due 2027-01-05)
transcript:
15:00:01 Jordan Lee: ok everyone, thanks for joining uh we wanted to kick off scoping for the in-vehicle assistant poc with Cygnus, i'm Jordan from Redwood AE, maya here is our solutions engineer, evan hopped on as well, um Maya over to you for a quick tech run before we dig in
15:00:15 Maya Patel: yeah thanks Jordan, hi Liam, Priya, Hannah, quick agenda — success criteria, workloads, benchmarks, integration points (sdk/openai compat), and timeline. we'll jot down action items at the end, um quick clarifying q: is this going to run on your cloud VPC or do you expect a private on-prem snap?
15:00:34 Liam O'Connor: most likely VPC peering to start, we have regulatory constraints around telematics PII so we'll want strict KMS control and audit logs. on-prem is a maybe down the road but not in scope for the first pilot.
15:00:46 Maya Patel: great, VPC peering + KMS is supported. we can run the benchmarks on Redwood Dedicated or in your Private VPC — we'll include both numbers.
15:00:55 Priya Desai: ok, success criteria from our side: 95th percentile response < 250ms for single-stream queries, throughput to handle 200 rps sustained during peak, and structural correctness for JSON outputs (we'll validate keys + types). cost is secondary but we want a per-month forecast for 1M active devices.
15:01:15 Jordan Lee: that lines up. quick note: our SDK and OpenAI-compatible endpoints support function calling and structured outputs — we can return JSON objects with a schema, or use tool-calling patterns if you need external enrichment.
15:01:30 Hannah Cole: for safety, we'll need audit trails (searchable), RBAC tied to our SSO, and SOC2 docs. also, support windows — 24/7 SLAs for incident triage would be nice to see in the proposal.
15:01:49 Maya Patel: we'll attach SOC2 report and the security brief in the follow-up. SLA details we'll outline in the Dedicated vs Private comparison.
15:02:05 Marco Ruiz: small thing, our fleet sends short VL telemetry bursts, so payloads can be 8–20 tokens on average but sometimes long assist flows are 200–400 tokens. we want batching to not increase latency beyond 10% for short flows.
15:02:24 Maya Patel: yep good point — we should test both micro-flows and long multi-turn flows. suggested benchmark profiles: micro (median 12 tokens, p95 latency target tight), session (avg 180 tokens, multi-turn with KV cache warmup), and multi-device bursts (spiky load 500–800 rps for 1–2 min).
15:02:48 Priya Desai: can Redwood's SDK do streaming to the client and incremental JSON assembly? we need partial responses to show on-device UI quickly.
15:03:02 Evan Chang: yes, we support streaming tokens plus structured output. there's a pattern we use: stream tokens, then an end-of-response structured JSON event. we'll share SDK snippets for both Node and Go.
15:03:17 Liam O'Connor: important: what about OpenAI-compat — do we need to change our current calls? we have existing code that hits gpt-style endpoints.
15:03:26 Jordan Lee: minimal changes — our /v1/compat endpoints accept familiar fields (prompt/messages, function_definitions). function calling semantics align with the OpenAI schema mostly; we'll call out a few Redwood-specific fields in the docs.
15:03:40 Priya Desai: function/tool calling — we want to call our enrichment microservice (latency ~30ms) and then write to our telemetry pipeline. can Redwood call back a function with structured args and give us the raw payload?
15:03:56 Maya Patel: yes that flow is supported. the runtime can return a function call payload, you run your service, then call the Redwood callback or supply the tool result back to the model. we'll show both synchronous and async patterns in the examples.
15:04:12 Hannah Cole: how do you validate structured output? we need schema enforcement — e.g., location {lat, lon}, confidence float, action string in set {navigate, alert, idle}.
15:04:24 Maya Patel: we recommend schema-first tests. Redwood Optimize can run a batch of prompts and validate output against JSON schemas, report F1/precision/recall for keys and types, and flag hallucinated fields. we'll include a simple test harness you can run locally.
15:04:44 Marco Ruiz: benchmark metrics list? p50/p90/p95, tails, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens?
15:04:52 Jordan Lee: exactly — p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens/sec, concurrency, memory/kv cache hit rate, plus end-to-end time including enrichment and downstream writes. cost projection we'll estimate for both Dedicated and Private.
15:05:10 Priya Desai: you'll run models quantized? we need accuracy numbers alongside speed.
15:05:17 Maya Patel: yes we'll include quantized variants and baseline FP32 numbers. we'll measure LM accuracy on your provided eval set and compare to OpenAI baseline you have.
15:05:28 Liam O'Connor: timeline — what's a realistic POC window? we want production-like data in a month if possible.
15:05:35 Jordan Lee: recommend 4-week sprint: week 0 (kickoff + environment + sample data ingestion), week 1 (benchmarks: micro/long/session), week 2 (integration: SDK + function calling flows), week 3 (tuning, cost forecast, final report & exec review).
15:05:52 Hannah Cole: do you need infra peering during week 0?
15:05:56 Marco Ruiz: yes we'll need firewall/IP allowlist and a test VPC subnet for egress.
15:06:02 Maya Patel: we'll provide IPs and peering docs; for Private we can provide a deployment image if you want to run in your network. we'll advise on bucket-level KMS integration.
15:06:17 Priya Desai: on observability, can we get per-token latency traces and token-level cost so we can attribute to device types?
15:06:26 Evan Chang: token-level costs and per-route latency breakdowns are available in Console. we'll add a per-device tag in the pilot so you can filter reports.
15:06:36 Liam O'Connor: during benchmarks, how long to run to get stable p95?
15:06:41 Maya Patel: depends on variability — for tails we recommend 30–60 minutes per profile under stable load, and a few short burst tests for spiky scenarios.
15:06:52 Priya Desai: one more — are there throttling and graceful degradation strategies? if our burst exceeds capacity we want automatic fallback to a smaller model variant.
15:07:01 Jordan Lee: yes, smart routing can fallback to lower-cost variants; we'll include canary and automatic fallback policies in the runbook.
15:07:12 Hannah Cole: ok great. can you walk through a sample bench plan now?
15:07:17 Maya Patel: quick sample — profile A (micro): 1 thread per device, 200 rps sustained for 10 min, median tokens 12. profile B (session): 50 concurrent sessions, avg 180 tokens, measure kv cache warm effect over time. profile C (burst): 800 rps for 2 min to see throttling and fallbacks. measure p50/p90/p95, tokens/sec, cost token, kv hit. we'll attach a spreadsheet with these rows.
15:07:46 Marco Ruiz: good — ensure the burst includes auth latencies too because our token service adds 20ms.
15:07:53 Maya Patel: we'll include an end-to-end column that runs with your auth flow.
15:07:58 Liam O'Connor: about streaming: if we stream partial JSON we need schema validation incrementally, is that feasible?
15:08:06 Evan Chang: streaming partial structures is tricky but possible — we can stream key-value chunks and then run a final schema validation at end-of-response. we'll show an example where UI renders progressive fields and marks them validated on final event.
15:08:22 Priya Desai: do you provide SDK instrumentation to emit traces?
15:08:26 Maya Patel: yep SDKs have hooks to propagate trace IDs and emit token-level events to Console.
15:08:34 Hannah Cole: service-level security — KMS integration modes? we need a hold of HSM options.
15:08:40 Jordan Lee: we support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed keys; HSM-backed KMS via your provider is possible in Private. we'll note that in the security doc.
15:08:54 Priya Desai: any gotchas for model size when doing on-device streaming?
15:08:59 Maya Patel: larger models increase cold-start latency; kv cache warms help for session flows. for streaming you want a model variant tuned for low-latency decode (quantized int8/int4) — we'll include recommended quantization profiles.
15:09:14 Marco Ruiz: for cost, show us both per-token and per-hour GPU cost for Dedicated — we need to compare to our in-house cluster $/GPU-hr.
15:09:21 Jordan Lee: will do; we'll include GPU-hr and token-based cost and an estimated amortized monthly bill for your expected fleet.
15:09:30 Liam O'Connor: success criteria recap before we wrap?
15:09:34 Priya Desai: p95 < 250ms for micro-flows; correctness > 98% for schema fields; handle 200 rps sustained and survive 800 rps bursts with fallback; provide end-to-end tracing and SSO/RBAC; and security docs.
15:09:50 Jordan Lee: thanks — that's a clear checklist. we'll align benchmarks and report against those metrics.
15:09:56 Maya Patel: next we should lock dates: we'll do kickoff 2027-01-05, hardware peering week of 2027-01-04, and first benchmark run week of 2027-01-11. does that work for you?
15:10:08 Liam O'Connor: yes that fits our schedule, we'll confirm infra availability by Friday.
15:10:12 Jordan Lee: great, i'll share the benchmark sheet now (drive.google.com/example-benchmark) and the security pack (redwood.com/security-pack.pdf).
15:10:20 Priya Desai: ok thanks all — quick Q: who is main contact for dev questions?
15:10:24 Jordan Lee: Maya will be SE lead, email maya@redwood.ai; Jordan for commercial.
15:10:30 Hannah Cole: perfect. any final notes?
15:10:34 Maya Patel: just that we'll include Node/Go SDK snippets, a sample function-calling flow, and a sample JSON schema validator in the repo.
15:10:42 Evan Chang: also include a tiny perf harness in the repo so you can reproduce our runs locally.
15:10:48 Liam O'Connor: appreciated. we'll look for the artifacts.
15:10:52 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, see you at kickoff.
15:10:56 [meeting end — 63 minutes]
